# LOGAN SOLAMAN — The Store Architect

> Shopify architecture specialist. Ten years engineering storefronts that compound: design, development, SEO, growth systems. Based in Hong Kong, working globally. Stores don't grow by accident — they grow by architecture.

- **Website**: https://logansolaman.com/
- **Canonical URL**: https://logansolaman.com/
- **Tagline**: THE STORE ARCHITECT — EST. 2016
- **Location**: Hong Kong; works globally
- **Languages**: 10 — English, 繁體中文, 简体中文, Español, العربية, Français, Português, 日本語, Tiếng Việt, 한국어
- **At a glance**: 10 years engineering · 15 storefronts built · 50 free merchant tools · 17 systems in the mission archive

## What this site is

A static portfolio with 17 individual case-study pages and 5 service pages for Logan Solaman's Shopify storefront architecture practice, plus a browser-based 50-tool armory. There is no build step at deploy time: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript served by GitHub Pages. Case and service pages are generated from `assets/js/site.js` and `locales/en.json` by `scripts/generate_pages.py`. The visual background is a WebGL2 matrix-rain shader built from a self-hosted katakana glyph atlas. All content is available in 10 languages via `locales/*.json`.

## Positioning

- **Stores don't grow by accident. They grow by architecture.**
- A storefront is a machine that turns attention into orders; every part either compounds or leaks.
- Approach: theme engineering that survives updates, apps that earn their keep, SEO wired into the structure rather than painted on, and growth loops measured in weeks, not vibes. If it can't be measured, it doesn't ship.
- Mission: give small brands the infrastructure of big ones — which is why the entire merchant toolset is free.

## Services — five modules, one compounding machine

1. **Storefront Engineering** — full Shopify builds from blank repo to launch day. Custom architecture tuned to brand and traffic, not a theme with a logo.
2. **Theme Customization** — deep Liquid/JS customization that keeps upgrade paths clean.
3. **App Development** — private apps, checkout extensions, integrations that earn their monthly cost.
4. **SEO & Velocity** — technical SEO built into the structure: Core Web Vitals, schema, international routing.
5. **Growth Operations** — post-launch conversion systems: CRO, analytics, A/B discipline, retention flows.

## Process — three steps

1. **Decrypt** — a free consult; find the real constraint.
2. **Blueprint** — custom plan with scope, stack and numbers.
3. **Launch & Tune** — ship, then iterate from day one of traffic.

## FAQ — 12 questions answered on the home page

What do you actually do · Is this just a theme with a logo · Can you work on an existing Shopify theme · What if the app I need doesn't exist · Is SEO bolted on at the end · What happens after launch · What does the first conversation cost · What do I get before any code is written · How do you decide what ships · Where are you based / do you work remotely · How quickly do you reply · Are the 50 tools really free.

Answers are drawn from the same service, process, manifesto and contact copy used elsewhere on the site. They are visible as HTML on the home page; no `FAQPage` structured data is emitted, because Google retired the FAQ rich result in May 2026.

## Contact

The consultation is free. Use the form at https://logansolaman.com/#contact — it builds a `mailto:` draft in the visitor's own mail client; the site stores nothing. Reply target is configured in `assets/js/site.js` (`CONTACT_EMAIL`).

## Interaction notes (for agents rendering the page)

- Keyboard: `1`–`7` jump to sections; `/` opens the command line; `[` `]` cycle color themes; `G` toggles the CRT grid; `M` toggles matrix rain; `T` glitches the title; `L` opens the language picker; `?` opens help; `ESC` closes.
- Command line supports: `about`, `services`, `cases`, `tools`, `process`, `faq`, `contact`, `theme`, `grid`, `rain`, `glitch`, `langs`, `lang <code>`, `filter <category>`, `ls`, `clear`, `help`.
- The home page ships its English copy as static HTML, so important content is available without JavaScript. The 17 case cards are rendered client-side from `assets/js/site.js` with names/descriptions from `locales/<lang>.json`, but each contains a real crawlable `<a>` to a static case-study page at `/cases/caseNN/`. A `<noscript>` block lists all 17 cases and 5 services as plain links. Case pages carry CreativeWork + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD; service pages carry Service + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD; `/tools/` carries WebApplication JSON-LD.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` renders a static shader frame and disables reveals.
- No analytics, no cookies, no tracking, no third-party storage. All fonts are self-hosted as local woff2; no third-party font requests.

## Content usage

Content signals are declared in `robots.txt`. Search indexing, AI input/grounding, and AI training are all permitted. `robots.txt` blocks nothing: CSS, JS and locale files must remain crawlable for Googlebot to render the page.

Note: Google Search does not use `llms.txt` for ranking or AI Overviews; this file is maintained for other services and agents that do consume it. It is not a substitute for crawlable HTML.
